Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Gatten and Lake Primary school a wonderful one–form entry school,
Apprenticeships
Admissions
Please click on the link below for more information on admissions.
The Ethos and the Environment
The children are at the heart of everything we do at Gatten and Lake, so there is no surprise, when we tell people the children dug the first turf for the new school building in 2013, and after 28 weeks the building was complete! We are very proud of the amazing building that we are so lucky to have and we respect the fantastic indoor and outdoor learning environments that are still growing and taking shape..
Arrange a Visit
Experience Gatten and Lake Primary School firsthand. Tailored to your child’s interests and admission stage, we offer visits year-round, from Reception to Year 6.
A Happy Learning Environment
Our mission is to ignite a lifelong passion for learning. By challenging the advanced and uplifting the less assured, we ensure each pupil realises their unique academic potential. Excellence for each child, each day.
We look forward to welcoming you to Gatten and Lake Primary School.

pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome
Welcome to Gatten and Lake Primary school a wonderful one–form entry school, which is situated in the town of Shanklin, adjacent to Lake. We are a coastal school, just a short distance from the beach but also in close proximity to the local woodland, America Woods, and next to the school site is the county ground.
The children are at the heart of everything we do at Gatten and Lake, so there is no surprise, when we tell people the children dug the first turf for the new school building in 2013, and after 28 weeks the building was complete! We are very proud of the amazing building that we are so lucky to have and we respect the fantastic indoor and outdoor learning environments that are still growing and taking shape.
The ‘Learning street’ is the central, focal point in the school, where there is continuous learning for classes, groups and individuals on a minute by minute basis. All of our classrooms lead off of the learning street; with Key stage one and two on parallel aspects.
Team work is an integral and key feature of success for both children and adults in the school as we all know each other so well which makes all transition stages so fluid and build positive strong relationships right from the start.
The education we provide is centred around the whole child, using the principles of the EYFS provision as a guide to continuing the development of these core skills throughout the Curriculum. ‘Excellence for each child, each day’ is our school vision which means we support every individual child’s needs to support and challenge where appropriate to help the child achieve and attain the best they possibly can.
We really hope that from the minute you walk through the door, you will feel the same passion for learning, for the children, as we do.
I sincerely welcome you to Gatten and Lake Primary school and look forward to meeting you soon to join in the fun with us.

SEND
Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
The Isle of Wight Council is committed to giving all children and young people high quality education that enables them to make progress and achieve well. For children and young people aged 0 to 25 with special educational needs or a disability, additional or specialist support may be needed to enable this. To support the process of identifying the range of provision and advice that is available, the Isle of Wight Local Authority have published a local offer. For more information about the Local Offer please use the following link: http://www.iwight.com/localoffer
Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilty Co-ordinator (SENDCo) is
Mrs L. RichardsYou can contact her by phoning the school office on 01983 869910 or via e-mail at laurarichards@gattenlakepri.iow.sch.uk
For more information about SEND provision at Gatten and Lake please see the links below:
If you have a child with special educational needs or disability you can also get advice from SENDIASS Isle of Wight. SENDIASS (IOW) offers free, impartial and confidential information, advice and support to parents, and carers of children and young people aged 0-25 with SEND as well as the young people themselves.

Blended and Remote Learning
At Gatten and Lake, we aim to deliver the highest-quality curriculum, so that our pupils know more and remember more. This means that everything we do to create the highest quality curriculum in school, must also align to our guiding principles for remote learning. We adopt a mixed model of asynchronous tasks, live lessons and pre-recorded lessons – all tailored to the needs of our children.
A mixed model of remote learning is considered more effective than using one method alone. Engagement increases when pupils feel part of the whole-school, whether they are working remotely, or in classrooms. Our teachers can also provide live feedback via Microsoft Teams in Key Stages 1 and 2.
